procedure.authority_basis: Authored against consulted operative descriptions and the safety literature listed in theatre/parameters.json (sources T1-T13). The step/microstep decomposition is this module's own, built to cognitive-task-analysis discipline (design/05): the published CTA of this procedure resolved 19 recalled steps into 97 microsteps (T5); the full published microstep list is not public, so this file authors an independent decomposition at the granularity the consulted operative sources support (census in MILESTONE-17.md). Nothing in this file is recalled unaided where a source could be consulted; anything not sourced is flagged in place.

decision_points.anchor: After microstep m2.2 (assessment of the gallbladder and inflammation).

choices.effect: Continue with the laparoscopic procedure as modelled.
choices.label: Proceed laparoscopically
choices.scoring: Neutral; correctness depends on findings, which the v1 scenario set does not grade.

choices.label: Convert to open
choices.scoring: Bailout-positive per design/05: choosing a bailout when findings warrant is scored positively, never as failure.

choices.effect: Bailout: stop, drain if indicated, refer to a hepatobiliary service.
choices.label: Abort and refer

decision_points.question: Do the operative findings permit proceeding laparoscopically?

decision_points.anchor: Declared by the operator when the Critical View of Safety cannot be achieved (evaluated at phase 4).

choices.effect: Continue dissecting in the hepatocystic triangle.
choices.label: Continue dissection
choices.scoring: Scored error err.no-bailout: the multi-society guideline recommends altering the operative strategy, preferably to subtotal cholecystectomy, when the CVS cannot be obtained (T3).

choices.effect: Perform phase 5 (intraoperative cholangiogram) to delineate the anatomy; the IOC group becomes required for this attempt.
choices.label: Intraoperative cholangiography

choices.effect: Bailout: subtotal cholecystectomy, fenestrating subtype (T4) — phase 6B replaces phases 5-7 requirements.
choices.label: Subtotal cholecystectomy, fenestrating
choices.scoring: Bailout-positive per design/05 and the preferred bailout in T3.

choices.effect: Bailout: subtotal cholecystectomy, reconstituting subtype (T4) — phase 6B with the closure microstep variant noted there.
choices.label: Subtotal cholecystectomy, reconstituting
choices.scoring: Bailout-positive; the reconstituting subtype carries a reoperation caveat (stones can re-form in the closed remnant, T4), surfaced in the debrief.

choices.effect: Pause and obtain senior/hepatobiliary assistance before proceeding.
choices.label: Call for senior help
choices.scoring: Positive judgment action; the attempt may then proceed by any route.

decision_points.question: The Critical View of Safety cannot be obtained. Which alternative strategy?

decision_points.anchor: Event-triggered: fires when a bleeding complication is computed.

choices.label: Compress and clear the field
choices.scoring: First-line; feeds the management score via time to control.

choices.effect: Clip or otherwise definitively control the bleeding structure (runner action: control).
choices.label: Definitive control of the vessel

choices.effect: Bailout: convert to open for vascular control.
choices.label: Convert to open
choices.scoring: Bailout-positive when bleeding is not controlled laparoscopically.

decision_points.question: Bleeding is not yet controlled. Escalate how?

decision_points.anchor: Event-triggered: fires when a bile duct injury is recognised.

choices.effect: Stop, do not attempt repair beyond drainage, call/refer to an experienced hepatobiliary team.
choices.label: Drain and refer to hepatobiliary team
choices.scoring: Guideline-preferred: referral of confirmed or suspected bile duct injury to an experienced hepatobiliary surgeon/team is a strong recommendation (T3).

choices.effect: Convert to open and repair in-house.
choices.label: Convert and repair
choices.scoring: Scored against the same guideline: appropriate only with hepatobiliary expertise present; the v1 scenario set does not model that expertise, so this choice scores below drain-refer.

choices.effect: Continue the cholecystectomy without addressing the injury.
choices.label: Continue regardless

decision_points.question: A bile duct injury is recognised. What now?

errors.consequence: Computed by the runner's misidentification resolution: the divided duct is the common bile duct — a Stewart-Way class III bile duct injury (the dominant injury pattern, 61% of the Way series). The attempt FAILS at the moment of division, regardless of all other scores (design/05 master rule).
errors.definition: Dividing a critical structure (cystic duct, cystic artery) before the Critical View of Safety is achieved and the structure is identified.

errors.consequence: The clip is placed on the common bile duct (Stewart-Way class I mechanism state). If the structure is then divided, err.divide-unidentified fires (class III). If the misplacement is recognised and the clip removed before division, the event is recorded as a near miss: heavily scored, not an automatic fail.
errors.definition: Applying a clip to the presumed cystic duct before the Critical View of Safety is achieved.

errors.consequence: Arterial haemorrhage is computed by the physiology engine from the moment of division until control; blood loss and MAP response are engine outputs, not script values.
errors.definition: Dividing the cystic artery before clips have been applied to it.

errors.consequence: When the target is the common hepatic or common bile duct, a thermal (class II mechanism) bile duct injury is recorded as a complication — lateral damage that presents as leak or late stricture. Otherwise a scored major error without a computed injury.
errors.definition: Applying electrocautery directly to a bile duct structure before that structure has been identified (Critical View achieved). Dissection energy used on peritoneum and triangle tissue in the authored microsteps is normal technique and does not fire this error; the class II mechanism is energy delivered to the duct itself.

errors.consequence: A bile leak complication is recorded (structural outcome; the physiology engine v0 has no biliary compartment, so no volume or pressure effect is computed — stated plainly in the debrief).
errors.definition: Dividing the cystic duct before clips have been applied to it.

errors.consequence: Process error; reduces the process score. No infection outcome is simulated in v1.
errors.definition: Prophylactic cefazolin started after incision, or more than the cited window before it.

errors.consequence: Process error; reduces the process score.
errors.definition: A WHO checklist phase (Sign In, Time Out, Sign Out) not performed at its integration point.

errors.consequence: Computed by the runner: the artery divided in the field is the replaced right hepatic artery — an unidentified critical structure divided. The attempt FAILS, and haemorrhage is computed at the replaced-artery rate until control.
errors.definition: In the replaced-right-hepatic-artery variant case, dividing the cystic artery without having first identified the variant vessel in the field.

errors.consequence: Haemorrhage from the uncontrolled branch is computed by the physiology engine until the branch is clipped; scored major error, recoverable — the contrast case to err.missed-variant: an identified-anatomy completeness failure, not a misidentification.
errors.definition: In the double-cystic-artery variant case, beginning liver-bed dissection while a second arterial branch remains uncontrolled.

errors.consequence: Judgment error in the analysis section of the debrief; the guideline alternative (subtotal cholecystectomy) is named.
errors.definition: At decision point dp2 (Critical View unobtainable), choosing to continue dissecting rather than altering strategy.

procedure.name: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy

microsteps.label: Review imaging and laboratory results; confirm the indication for cholecystectomy
Confirm consent and operative plan, including anticipation of biliary and arterial variants
Confirm team, resource tier and equipment plan for the case
microsteps.note: Resource tiers per design/05 (basic / limited / enhanced / maximal); the tier is recorded with the attempt, not scored in v1.

microsteps.label: Administer cefazolin 2 g IV within 60 minutes before incision (3 g if >=120 kg)
Apply venous thromboembolism prophylaxis per protocol
microsteps.note: Process step as carried in the design/05 setup list; no agent or dose is asserted — none was consulted for this module.

microsteps.label: Position the patient supine with arms tucked; displays positioned for the American configuration
Equipment check: laparoscope and camera, insufflator, suction, energy source
WHO Sign In completed before induction of anaesthesia
WHO Time Out completed before skin incision
Infraumbilical skin incision
Dissect subcutaneous tissue to the fascia
Incise the fascia
Enter the peritoneum under direct vision (Hasson open technique)
Place and secure the Hasson cannula
Insufflate CO2 to a pneumoperitoneum of 15 mmHg
Insert the 30-degree laparoscope; confirm intraperitoneal position and survey the abdomen
Select the epigastric port site, about 2 cm below the liver edge and right of the falciform ligament
Insert the 10 mm epigastric port under vision
Insert the 5 mm mid-clavicular port under vision
Insert the 5 mm anterior-axillary port under vision
Position in reverse Trendelenburg with left-side tilt
Confirm all ports and instruments before proceeding
Systematic abdominal exploration
Assess the gallbladder, inflammation severity and adhesions
Grasp the fundus and retract cephalad over the liver dome
Grasp the infundibulum (Hartmann's pouch) and retract caudolaterally to open the hepatocystic triangle
microsteps.note: Traction geometry is the substrate of the classic misidentification: it tents the common bile duct into line with the cystic duct (T1).

microsteps.label: Adhesiolysis where required to expose the gallbladder and triangle
Incise the peritoneum over the infundibulum, anterior aspect
Incise the peritoneum over the infundibulum, posterior aspect
Clear fat and fibrous tissue from the anterior hepatocystic triangle
Clear fat and fibrous tissue from the posterior hepatocystic triangle
Expose the junction of the gallbladder neck and the cystic duct
Trace the cystic duct continuously into the gallbladder neck
Expose the cystic artery within the hepatocystic triangle
Trace the cystic artery onto the gallbladder wall
Create a window between the cystic duct and the cystic artery
Create a window between the cystic artery and the liver edge
Confirm the triangle is cleared: framed by the common hepatic duct medially and the liver edge above, traversed only by the cystic duct and cystic artery
Survey the triangle and the duct course for additional or replaced vessels
microsteps.note: The variant checkpoint: a replaced right hepatic artery ascends posterolateral to the common bile duct and posterior to the portal vein (T12 variant record) and can cross this field.

microsteps.label: Control minor ooze within the triangle
Re-inspect the triangle from the posterior aspect with the angled scope
Confirm no other tubular structure enters the operative field
Separate the lower third of the gallbladder from the liver bed
Expose the cystic plate across the gallbladder-liver interface
Demonstrate the cystic duct entering the gallbladder
Demonstrate the cystic artery entering the gallbladder
Confirm two and only two structures enter the gallbladder
Pre-clip pause: the Critical View is verbalised and confirmed with the team before any clip is applied
Clip the cystic duct close to the gallbladder neck
Incise the cystic duct partway (ductotomy)
Milk the duct contents toward the ductotomy
Insert the cholangiogram catheter
Secure the catheter
Inject contrast under fluoroscopy
Confirm the intrahepatic and extrahepatic ducts opacify and contrast flows freely into the duodenum
Check the cholangiogram for filling defects and extravasation
Remove the catheter
Clip the cystic duct below the ductotomy
Apply two clips to the cystic artery on the patient side
Apply a clip to the cystic artery on the gallbladder side
Divide the cystic artery between clips
Apply two clips to the cystic duct on the patient side
Apply a clip to the cystic duct on the gallbladder side
Divide the cystic duct between clips
Identify the second cystic artery branch entering the gallbladder
Clip the second cystic artery branch
Divide the second cystic artery branch between clips

steps.name: Second cystic artery branch (variant configuration only)

microsteps.label: Open the gallbladder at the fundus and evacuate bile
Extract all stones from the gallbladder lumen
Excise the free peritonealised gallbladder wall, leaving the portion shielding the hepatocystic triangle in place
Close the cystic duct orifice from inside the remnant (purse-string suture)
Confirm the fenestrating configuration: remnant left open with no sealed lumen (for the reconstituting choice at dp2, the remnant is instead closed and the reformation caveat applies)
Place a drain to the gallbladder fossa

steps.name: Subtotal cholecystectomy branch (bailout, replaces phases 5-7 when chosen at dp2)

phases.name: Liver bed, haemostasis and final inspection

microsteps.label: Dissect the gallbladder off the liver bed in the cystic plate plane
Maintain haemostasis of the liver bed
Inspect the liver bed for bleeding
Inspect the divided duct and artery and their clips; check for bile leak
Irrigate and suction the operative field
Place a closed drain to the gallbladder fossa
Place the gallbladder in a retrieval bag
Extract the bagged gallbladder via the umbilical port
Desufflate under vision and remove all ports
Close the fascia at the umbilical 10 mm site
Close the fascia at the epigastric 10 mm site
Close the skin
WHO Sign Out completed before the patient leaves the operating room

review.status: UNMET — design/05 and design/10 require at least two named independent expert reviewers with Delphi sign-off before this procedure's content status can rise above dual-sourced-draft. No reviewers exist for this project; the gate is reported as unmet, never satisfied on paper.

criteria.definition: The hepatocystic triangle is cleared of fat and fibrous tissue. The common bile duct and common hepatic duct do not have to be exposed.
criteria.name: Hepatocystic triangle cleared

criteria.definition: The lower one-third of the gallbladder is separated from the liver to expose the cystic plate.
criteria.name: Cystic plate exposed

criteria.definition: Two and only two structures are seen entering the gallbladder.
criteria.name: Two and only two structures

safety_gates.enforcement: The runner evaluates this gate at every clip and divide action on a critical structure. A divide action taken while the gate is unachieved does not clip the intended anatomy: it resolves through the misidentification model (err.divide-unidentified) and fails the attempt. Dependent steps (phases 5, 6 and 7) are the gate's unlock set.
safety_gates.name: Critical View of Safety
safety_gates.statement: The Critical View of Safety must be achieved AND demonstrated (all three criteria, via the microsteps that demonstrate them) before any clip is applied to, or any structure is divided in, the hepatocystic triangle.

criteria.definition: Before clipping or transecting the cystic duct or artery, the operator pauses and the team confirms the Critical View of Safety has been achieved.
criteria.name: Momentary pause and team confirmation before clipping/transecting

safety_gates.enforcement: Scored checkpoint (microstep m4.6), not a second blocking gate in v1: the blocking gate is the Critical View itself. Omitting the pause forfeits the safety point and is named in the debrief analysis.
safety_gates.name: Pre-clip pause (culture of safety)

checklist.derivation: Completed required microsteps / required microsteps for the attempt's configuration (variant and bailout configurations change the required set by the rules in variants[] and decision_points dp2). Reported as a percentage and as counts.

management.applies: Only when a complication was computed; otherwise reported as not applicable.
management.derivation: Recognition of the complication (2), definitive control achieved where control applies (1), escalation appropriate to the event (1), definitive plan consistent with the guideline (1).

physiology.derivation: Computed from the physiology engine run, never from the trace script: time-below-threshold component (3/2/1/0 by the rubric bands in theatre parameters), nadir MAP component (>= threshold 2; 55 to threshold 1; below 55 0), blood-loss component (bands in theatre parameters: 2/1/0).

process.derivation: One point each: WHO Sign In, WHO Time Out, WHO Sign Out, prophylaxis inside the cited window, Step 0 planning microsteps complete.

safety_gate.derivation: One point per Critical View criterion demonstrated before the first clip or divide action (3), plus one for the pre-clip pause performed before the first clip (1). Gate violations are additionally recorded as errors and, for division, fail the attempt — the points never offset the fail rule.

scoring.notes: No composite score is computed: design/05 defines components, not a weighting, and inventing weights would violate the precision law. GOALS (T8) and OSATS (T9) are carried as rubric data for observed-performance rating in the shells; a headless scripted runner has no observed performance to rate, so both are reported as NOT POPULATED in v1 debriefs rather than estimated. Scores are formative only (validity label below) until construct evidence exists.

goals.status: rubric data; not populated by the headless runner

osats.status: rubric data; not populated by the headless runner

scoring.verdict_rule: FAIL if any critical-fail error fired (err.divide-unidentified or err.missed-variant); otherwise PASS. Bailout choices at decision points never cause a fail and score positively (design/05).

structures.note: Digestive clinical record: parts (fundus, body, neck, Hartmann's pouch), capacity 30-50 mL, blood supply text naming the cystic artery as a branch of the right hepatic artery.
Digestive clinical record for the liver; the liver bed and cystic plate references resolve here and to region.cystic-plate.
Digestive clinical record carrying the biliary tree and the named absence of a common bile duct concept.
Digestive inventory record with the gallbladder geometry set.
Digestive inventory record (FJ3625) — the cystic duct as modelled geometry.
Digestive inventory record; bounds the hepatocystic triangle medially.
Digestive inventory record; upstream biliary anatomy referenced by the cholangiogram step.
Digestive inventory record; upstream biliary anatomy referenced by the cholangiogram step.
Cardiovascular clinical record; the standard arterial axis from which the cystic artery typically arises (via the right hepatic artery).
Cardiovascular clinical record.
Cardiovascular clinical record; branch point of the hepatic artery proper.
Cardiovascular clinical record; origin of the common hepatic artery.
Cardiovascular clinical record; the origin of the replaced right hepatic artery in variant 1.
Cardiovascular inventory record — the modelled right hepatic artery geometry (no separate clinical record exists under a plain right-hepatic id).
Cardiovascular clinical record; the replaced right hepatic artery ascends posterior to it (variant record).
Cardiovascular variant record (Michels type III), prevalence 8.7-11.0% in the module's two cited sources. Basis of procedure variant 1.

The cystic artery has NO BodyParts3D concept and NO cardiovascular clinical record (probe-verified in Milestone 5). Its anatomy here is sourced from T11 (origin from the right hepatic artery in 89% of cases, CI 85-92; mean diameter 1.91 mm) and from the organ.gallbladder record's supply text. Every reference to it in this procedure resolves to this absence note, per the task rule.

The second branch of a double cystic artery. No Body Model record exists for the cystic artery at all (see artery.cystic); the variant anatomy is sourced from T11 (double cystic artery 13%, CI 11-16%).

The common bile duct has NO BodyParts3D concept (Milestone 11): the biliary tree is otherwise modelled (cystic, common hepatic, left and right hepatic ducts), and the digestive record dig.biliary-tree carries the common bile duct as a named absence. It appears in this procedure only as the structure injured in the misidentification resolution — which is precisely the anatomy the Body Model most needs and does not yet have; the gap is stated, not papered over.

A surgical field, not an organ: bounded by the cystic duct, the common hepatic duct and the inferior edge of the liver (T2). No Body Model record exists for surgical regions; references resolve to this definition.
The connective-tissue plate of the gallbladder bed, continuous with the liver's fibrous capsule. No dedicated Body Model record; the underlying anatomy resolves to organ.liver and organ.gallbladder.
The outpouching of the gallbladder neck. Carried as a named part inside the organ.gallbladder clinical record; no separate Body Model record exists.

Procedure-local handle for the variant vessel in variant 1; resolves to the Body Model variant record variant.replaced-right-hepatic-artery-from-sma (systems/cardiovascular/variants.json). Listed as an absence-kind entry because the handle itself is not a record id; its resolution target is the variant record, checked by tools/theatre_check.py.

validity.consequences: Scores are formative feedback only; no credentialing or progression decision may rest on them.
validity.internal_structure: Component scores derived from the procedure model and the physiology engine state; arithmetic independently recomputed by tools/theatre_check.py.
validity.label: formative-only
validity.relations: No known-groups or predictive evidence exists yet; none is claimed.
validity.response_process: Scripted traces in v1; observed-performance response processes (GOALS/OSATS rating) are future shell work.

gate_modifications: Microstep m3.12 (variant survey) is the discovery point; the runner requires an explicit identify action on artery.replaced-rha before any cystic artery division microstep in this configuration.

If the cystic artery is divided without that identification, the division resolves to the replaced right hepatic artery (err.missed-variant): attempt FAIL plus computed haemorrhage at the replaced-artery rate.
variants.name: Replaced right hepatic artery from the superior mesenteric artery (Michels type III)

gate_modifications: Step 6.3 microsteps (identify, clip, divide the second branch) become required in this configuration.
Beginning liver-bed dissection (phase 7) with the second branch uncontrolled computes haemorrhage from that branch until it is clipped (err.uncontrolled-branch).
variants.name: Double cystic artery
variants.prevalence: 13% (95% CI 11-16%) (T11 meta-analysis). Not present in the Milestone 5 cardiovascular records — the cystic artery has no Body Model concept at all; this variant is therefore sourced at theatre level with the absence stated, exactly as the precision law requires.
